fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Open Terrain; Dense Vegetation
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the turn-in point, particularly in low-light or smoky conditions.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Remove or cut back overhanging branches along the driveway to allow ladder trucks and tall emergency vehicles to travel the full length without interference.
• Create a turnaround area near the main residence so emergency vehicles are not forced to back out the full length of the driveway.
• Keep the area around the detached structure clear of dense vegetation to allow responders to reach and work around it without being blocked.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move on foot between the two buildings.
• Post the property address visibly at the road and again near the main residence to help responders confirm location after traveling the length of the driveway.
• Maintain a clear staging area near the main residence large enough for multiple emergency vehicles to park and operate without blocking the driveway.
• Keep the access drive free of parked vehicles, stored equipment, and debris so the full length remains passable at all times.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Vegetation Near Structure; Grass Cover; Mixed Vegetation; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Limited Rear Access; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the structure on any side where vegetation contacts or nearly touches the walls or roof.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between tree canopies and the building.
• Mow or cut grass around the structure, especially during dry periods when grass dries out and becomes more flammable.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from within the mixed vegetation areas closest to the structure.
• Thin shrubs in the scattered areas near the structure so they are not grouped tightly together.
• Clear overhanging branches from any trees positioned directly above or adjacent to the roof and gutters.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation on both sides so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it remains visible to emergency responders approaching from the road.
• Clear a path along the rear of the structure wide enough for a person to walk through and inspect the building.
• Remove any dead shrubs or dry woody debris from the areas directly behind the structure where rear access is limited.
• Keep grass cut short along the edges of the driveway and access route to reduce the chance of fire spreading along the roadway toward the structure.
